items.prompt: Tap the square where a black piece could settle with a black pawn behind it and no white pawn able to attack it.

claims.statement: The only outpost for Black is d4.

hints: Look for a square on White's side of the board.
A black pawn must defend it, and no white pawn may be able to attack it, now or later.
It is the square behind White's d5 pawn.
items.explain: The black pawn on e5 defends d4, and White has no pawn on c3 or e3 that could ever attack it. It is the only such square for Black in this position.

hints: Black's plan is the f-break. What stands in its way?
A knight move can clear the f6 square or prepare the break, and a quiet pawn move waits.
The knight to d7, or a quiet pawn move such as a5, b6 or c6.
items.explain: Moving the knight (Nd7 or Ne8) prepares the f-break, and quiet moves such as a5, b6, c6 or Kh8 are all within a few centipawns of the best. The rushed breaks ...b5 and ...g5, and the capture ...Nxe4, lose material at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.b7b5: The pawn attacks c4, but White takes it with cxb5 and the engine reads White clearly ahead.
feedback_by_move.g6g5: The bishop on c1 attacks the pawn on g5 and nothing defends it, so the storm starts by losing a pawn.
feedback_by_move.f6e4: The knight takes a pawn that is defended: White wins a piece for the pawn.

hints: Which white pawn can Black attack with a pawn move on the f-file?
The knight is already on d7, so the f-pawn can move.
The f-pawn goes to f5; a quiet move also does no harm.
items.explain: With the knight on d7 the f-pawn is free: ...f5 attacks e4 and is the plan's break; quiet moves such as ...b6 or ...Kh8 are within a few centipawns. The other pawn advances (...g5, ...b5, ...c5) are worse by well over a third of a pawn at depth 16, and ...g5 and ...b5 lose material.

feedback_by_move.c7c5: It does not fit the plan, and the engine gives White a larger edge.
feedback_by_move.g6g5: The pawn storm starts before the f-break; the pawn on g5 is attacked by the bishop on e3 and is loose.
feedback_by_move.b7b5: It loses a pawn to cxb5.

hints: The centre is now locked. Where does the c6 knight belong?

The knight goes to e7.
items.explain: After 8.d5 the knight on c6 has no good square on the queenside; e7 takes it to the kingside where the f-break is prepared. ...Nd4 and ...Nb4 are worse by about a third of a pawn or more.

feedback_by_move.c6d4: The engine gives White a larger edge after this knight move.
feedback_by_move.c6b4: The engine gives White a larger edge after this knight move.

hints: Here the pawn on d4 is not yet on d5. Is the centre locked?
When the centre is open, the pieces matter more than the pawn plans.
Play ...Ng4, ...Re8 or ...Bg4; do not copy the previous move.
items.explain: After 8.Be3 the centre can open, and the knight retreat ...Ne7 does nothing about it: White takes on e5 and keeps a clear advantage. The plan of the locked centre does not apply until White commits to d5.

feedback_by_move.c6e7: With the centre not locked, this retreat misses ...exd4 and the pawn structure: White can take on e5 and the engine gives White much more.

items.prompt: White to move. The b-pawn stands on b4. White plays c5. Does the pawn push keep White's edge? Choose, or step back to the board above if you want an example first.

claims.statement: After c5 the engine (depth 16) reads White ahead.
One white pawn, the pawn on b4, defends the pawn on c5.
After c5 dxc5 the engine (depth 16) reads White clearly ahead: bxc5 follows.

hints: Count the pieces and pawns that defend the pawn on c5 now.

Yes. The break is supported by the b-pawn.
items.explain: The pawn on b4 takes back if Black captures on c5, so the break is supported and the engine reads White ahead at depth 16. Compare the last position: the same push with the b-pawn on b2 has no support.

items.prompt: White to move. Choose a sound move.

claims.statement: The engine (depth 16) prefers f3; every accepted move is within 45 centipawns of the best move.

hints: Count the defenders of e4 after Black's last move.

The f-pawn goes to f3.
items.explain: f3 adds a second defender to e4 and keeps the centre locked. Capturing on f5 opens the position and hands Black the better game, and f4 weakens e4 and the king.

feedback_by_move.e4f5: Taking opens the centre and the knight recaptures with a route to d4; the engine gives Black the better game.
feedback_by_move.f2f4: It lets Black take, and the centre opens on Black's terms; the engine rates it clearly worse than f3.
